title: Chronic Sublethal Injury in a Critically Endangered Flapper Skate (Dipturus intermedius): In Situ Observations Compatible With Trawl Capture
content:
ABSTRACT

Sublethal effects of bycatch in elasmobranchs are typically assessed using short-term survival metrics, yet post-release pathology remains poorly documented. We report in situ observations of a flapper skate (Dipturus intermedius) in the northeast Atlantic exhibiting skeletal and soft-tissue abnormalities—vertebral deformation, truncation of the tail, orbital protrusion and an epidermal hyperplastic lesion on the rostrum—while maintaining normal behaviour. While not conclusive, these co-occurring pathologies are compatible with trawl capture. This article serves to highlight the need to consider sublethal injury, rather than binary survival, in assessments of fisheries impact for threatened elasmobranchs.
